newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST -- U.S. August PPI seen contained.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -- U.S. August PPI seen contained.

text.p: Wholesale prices probably remained steady in August despite signs of a tighter labor market and higher wages, U.S. experts said.
"PPI inflation remains very well subdued," said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZW Securities Inc.
U.S. economists polled by Reuters forecast a modest 0.1 percent gain in the August Producer Price Index (PPI), which the Labor Department releases Thursday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
Excluding the volatile food and energy component, PPI is expected to rise 0.1 percent.

"Even though the labor numbers are suggesting it (inflation) is going to be a problem over the next quarter, and maybe into (early) next year the bottom line is that inflation is still not a problem," Best added.

Best forecast a modest 0.1 percent increase in the overall August PPI figure and a 0.2 percent rise in the core rate. He said the PPI number would have to register an increase of at least 0.4 percent to elicit a market response.
U.S. economists expect the food component to increase as higher grain prices of the last few months filter into food prices. Energy prices are expected to ease off a bit.
Less pressure on energy prices was expected because of unusually cool summer leading resulting in less need for air conditioning use in the Northeast.
"Energy having reached its peak right around the Memorial Day weekend has eased off, allowing demand for energy to ease so we expect prices to be off a bit," BZW's Best explained.
Auto and truck prices, which make up 18 percent of the index, may be pressured higher due to seasonal factors, economists said.

"There may be some upward pressure in auto and truck prices because of some seasonals but I think that may be more of an issue next month," said Michelle Laughlin, Treasury market strategist at Prudential Securities Inc.
Laughlin predicted a slight gain of 0.1 percent in the overall PPI number, and an identical rise in the core rate.
"I don't see any trouble spots I expect trend increases across most major sectors," Laughlin said.
However, Laughlin added, "There may be some risks that pipeline costs or leading inflation indicators, will be less market favorable this month."
The Prudential stategist cited the recent sharp runup in raw material prices reported in the Journal of Commerce Index.

While market participants will look at Thursday's PPI report for any hint of inflation pressures at the whole sale level, they will especially key in to Friday's release of the August Consumer Price Index (CPI) for a reading on inflation at the consumer level.
Economists said CPI is seen as a key to Federal Open Market Committee meeting deliberations at its next monetary policy-setting meeting scheduled on September 24.

"A higher-than-expected PPI figure would certainly raise concerns about a higher-than-expected CPI report and in general heighten expectations of at least a 25 basis point increase in the funds rate at the next meeting," Laughlin said.
